texts: mixed: "clear" and "mild" both land on the night with its tense and date, but two parts of the frame go badly - "the night of the autumn equinox" becomes a possession link (the night belongs to the equinox) where the phrase only says which night it was, and "day 0 of Year 1" drops into the day-of-month slot, so it will not order against other dates. Recasting the weather impersonally with an anaphoric time fixes the of-phrase: "In Year 1, the autumn equinox occurred on day 0, and it was clear and mild that night." The epoch-style day index still has no proper calendar term, so if day ordering matters downstream a named month or weekday would carry it.

bad: "about twenty-five" has no licensed carrier - the count slot takes a plain integer, and the bound and vague-phrase forms do not fit a hedged exact figure - so the number either lands ill-typed (as it does now) or is dropped entirely, leaving the rule with moths but no count. Drop the hedge: "Keepers counted twenty-five nightmoths at each lantern of the Cliff Path." If the vagueness matters, a stated range ("between twenty and thirty nightmoths") is carried properly as two bounds.
good. the crowd is typed both as a crowd and as a crowd of nightmoths, the gathering stays collective as it should, and the East Row gets both its name and its kind.
good. the three sky-cats, the count, the descent and the cliff-spires as the source all land, plus a per-cat rule so an individual cat's descent is derivable.
good. the hunt reuses the same three cats and the same nightmoth crowd from the earlier sentences, with the East Row as the place and a per-cat rule alongside.
good. the crowd's position at the East Row and its shrinking both attach to the crowd already introduced.

mixed: the seven are correctly recorded as a subset of the East Row crowd counted at the third watch, but "at the East Row" yields no atom of its own - it is read as saying which nightmoths, not where the keepers were. If you meant the place of the counting, front it: "At the East Row, keepers counted seven of the nightmoths at the third watch."

bad: the survivors are minted as a brand-new group with no link to the hunted crowd, and - unlike descending, hunting, fleeing and reaching in this same passage - the surviving is not handed down to individual moths, so neither "which moths survived" nor "did this moth survive" can resolve. Writing it as a partitive of the crowd fixes the link and matches how sentence 7 already handles "seven of the nightmoths": "Some of the nightmoths survived the hunt."
good. the flight, the surviving moths and the Hollows as the destination all land, with a per-moth rule alongside.

bad: "reached the Hollows" is recorded as a destination rather than as the verb's own object, on both the event and its per-moth rule, so it stores the same thing the previous sentence's "fled to the Hollows" stores and a question about what was reached will not match. Saying the arrival explicitly makes the destination reading the correct one: "The surviving nightmoths arrived at the Hollows."
